title: Throughput & Latency Sparklines for Sessionized Workloads (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working collateral piece intended to help product and SRE stakeholders understand the tradeoffs between throughput, tail latency, and token cost for sessionized (multi-turn) conversational workloads. Focus is on quick visual primitives (sparklines & small ASCII charts) that we can drop into a slide or README. Goal: give product managers and solutions engineers simple heuristics for picking batching/cache profiles and quantization knobs for different SLA tiers.

Test matrix (high level)
- Workloads: short-chat (avg 4 turns, 40 tokens/turn), long-chat (avg 20 turns, 80 tokens/turn), search-assist (single long prompt, 300 tokens)
- Models: open-small (7B fp16), baseline-medium (13B fp16), quantized-medium (13B int8), large (34B fp16)
- HW: node-a100 (A100-80GB static), node-h100 (H100 dynamic), cpu-backfill for opportunistic slots
- Serving modes: windowed-batching (1s window), opportunistic-slots (fill-to-n), prewarmed-sessions (idle keepalive 10m), kv-cache enabled/disabled
- Metrics: P50/P90/P95/P99 token latency (ms), tokens/sec per GPU, $ per 1M tokens (approx), cache hit-rate by prefix

Micro-sparkline legend (for inline text use):
- ▂▁▁▂▃▅▇ = low -> high latency over session
- $$$ = cost gradient (low -> high) represented qualitatively

Representative results (aggregated across 3 runs each; numbers are illustrative, see scripts/bench-sessionized for raw CSVs)

1) Short-chat (4 turns, 40 tokens/turn)
- 13B fp16, A100, windowed-batching(1s), kv-cache ON
  - throughput: 320 tokens/sec per GPU
  - P50/P90/P95/P99 per-token lat (ms): 10 / 28 / 45 / 130
  - cost: ~$2.8 per 1M tokens
  - cache hit-rate (prefix): 62%
  - sparkline (lat across session turns): ▂▂▃▅▇ (rising tail as context grows)

- 13B int8 quant, A100, opportunistic, kv-cache ON
  - throughput: 540 tokens/sec per GPU (higher batching efficiency)
  - P50/P90/P95/P99: 12 / 36 / 70 / 250 (notice higher tail)
  - cost: ~$1.6 per 1M tokens
  - cache hit-rate: 60%
  - sparkline: ▂▃▅▆▇ (steeper tail)

Takeaway: for short-chat at low-to-mid SLOs, quantized models + opportunistic batching save ~40–50% cost but increase P99 significantly — acceptable for best-effort tiers. If P99>200ms is unacceptable, prefer fp16 with moderate windowing and keep kv-cache ON.

2) Long-chat (20 turns, 80 tokens/turn)
- 13B fp16, H100, prewarmed-sessions (10m keepalive), kv-cache ON
  - throughput: 720 tokens/sec (amortized across turns)
  - per-token latency P50/P90/P95/P99: 9 / 22 / 38 / 95
  - cost: ~$2.1 per 1M tokens (higher throughput on H100 reduces unit cost)
  - cache hit-rate: 78% (higher due to repeated prefixes)
  - sparkline (per-turn aggregated latency): ▂▂▂▂▂ (flat — warm path benefits)

- 13B int8, H100, opportunistic, kv-cache OFF
  - throughput: 980 tokens/sec
  - P50/P90/P95/P99: 15 / 52 / 120 / 420
  - cost: ~$1.1 per 1M tokens
  - cache hit-rate: 0%
  - sparkline: ▂▃▅▇▇ (rising sharply once cache absent)

Takeaway: sessionized workloads with high intra-session repetition benefit substantially from enabling kv-cache and keeping sessions warm. For long-lived sessions, fp16 on faster HW (H100) + keepalive gives both lower tail latency and moderate cost. Quantization without cache can give big cost wins but risks huge P99s as sequence length grows.

3) Search-assist (single long prompt, 300 tokens)
- 34B fp16, A100, batch-size 1 (low batching), kv-cache N/A
  - P50/P90/P95/P99 total-response (ms): 350 / 620 / 780 / 1050
  - tokens/sec: 280
  - cost: ~$9.6 per 1M tokens
  - sparkline: ▃▅▅▅▇ (high cost/latency across the board)

- 13B int8, A100, windowed-batching(1s), kv-cache N/A
  - P50/P90/P95/P99: 420 / 980 / 1500 / 2100
  - tokens/sec: 460
  - cost: ~$3.2 per 1M tokens
  - sparkline: ▅▇▇▇▇ (worse tails for large single requests)

Takeaway: for single large prompts, model capacity dominates. Quantized medium models can be cheaper but have much worse long-tail latency; for strict latency SLAs pick a higher-capacity fp model or split prompts at application-level.

Quick CDF comparisons (ASCII-style, normalized latency buckets)
- Example: short-chat, fp16 vs int8 (normalized counts across lat buckets)
  fp16: |#####-----| (P90 at bucket 2, P99 in bucket 5)
  int8: |###-------| (P90 in bucket 3, large mass in bucket 5 long tail)

Operational heuristics (rules-of-thumb)
- If P99 < 200ms required: prefer fp16 models, H100 when possible, keep kv-cache ON and prewarm sessions for expected repeat sessions > 3 turns.
- If cost is primary and P99 can be relaxed: quantized int8 with opportunistic batching and short keepalive (or zero) gives 30–60% cost reduction. Use cache only if repeat prefixes expected.
- For long single prompts: prefer larger fp models; batching benefits are limited because requests are large and rare.

Recommended artifacts to add next (TODO)

- Raw CSV exporter in scripts/bench-sessionized -> /artifacts/sessionized/ with naming convention {model}-{hw}-{mode}-{date}.csv
- Add a simple dashboard tile: "Sessionized P99 vs cost per 1M tokens" with model and kv-cache filter.

Open questions / known caveats
- These runs used synthetic user traces built from production logs but not exact privacy-preserving sampling; need a follow-up run with true sampled sessions (requires infra ticket JIRA-ING-1310).
- Quantized int8 numbers are sensitive to kernel selection; observed big variance across driver versions — tag results with driver/kernel/torch-onnx versions.
- We didn't test partial caching strategies (e.g., only caching last-k turns) — probable middle ground worth exploring.

Appendix: quick ASCII glossary
- kv-cache: prefix attention cache used across session turns
- opportunistic batching: fill available slots until either slot full or timeout then dispatch
- windowed-batching: fixed-time window for batching requests (e.g., 1000ms)
